key: Far went our earliest invocation of the Gods, and won us glories that can never be surpassed. They who could not ascend the ship of sacrifice, sink down in desolation, trembling with alarm.
s: Between bidding Indra sit on the holy grass and wishing the evil-hearted far away, the singer sets two fates at the sacrifice side by side; Sāyaṇa, on 10.44.6, reads those left behind as evildoers without Indra’s grace, brought low by debt, and Yāska, Nirukta 5.25, as those who stayed in this very world, or in debt.
src: Sāyaṇa on Rig Veda 10.44.6, sa.wikisource revision 328215 (2021); Yāska, Nirukta 5.25, in Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1921)

evidence.words: ये त्वत्प्रसादरहिता जनाः “यज्ञियां यज्ञसंबन्धिनीम् । यज्ञमयीमित्यर्थः । “नावम् “आरुहम् आरोढुं “न “शेकुः न शक्नुवन्ति “ते “केपयः कुत्सितपूयकर्माणः पापकर्माणो जनाः “ईर्मैंव ऋणेनैव “न्यविशन्त नीचैरविशन्त । अधोगतिं प्राप्ता इत्यर्थः … Now those, who were not able to ascend the ship of sacrifice, remained here, i.e. in this very place, or in debt, or in this world.
evidence.gloss: Sāyaṇa: those people without your (Indra’s) grace could not ascend the ship made of sacrifice; they, kepayaḥ, doers of foul deeds, people of evil acts, sank down by debt itself, went low, that is, reached the downward course … Yāska (Sarup): those who could not ascend the ship of sacrifice remained here, in this very place, or in debt, or in this world.

reason: Problem holds. Re-opened packet.js veda 110 --verse 10.44.6. Sāyaṇa (sa.wikisource rev 328215) glosses those who could not board as tvatprasādarahitā janāḥ (without Indra’s grace), kepayaḥ as pāpakarmāṇo janāḥ (evildoers), īrmaiva as ṛṇenaiva (by debt), nyaviśanta as nīcair aviśanta, adhogatiṃ prāptāḥ (brought low); Yāska, Nirukta 5.25 (Sarup, same packet, and cited by Sāyaṇa himself: ṛṇenaiva ... asminn eva loka iti vā), leaves alternatives: remained here, in this very place, or in debt, or in this world. A genuine difference, named not resolved; by2 yaska eases the Sāyaṇa spread. Plain clause replaced, as the revision refuter asked, with context from the hymn itself (v. 5 bids Indra sit on the holy grass, v. 7 wishes the evil-hearted far away) and states the contrast of fates at the sacrifice without paraphrasing the key verse or using the commentators’ agentive gloss. verse.js ok (10.44.6, [880,6]); entry-check ok on scratch/critic3-110.json, no errors or warns; under the 60-word cap.
